$comment: Corpus manifest for the PQ rag component: the official regulatory-guidance texts the gold questions in gold-dataset.json ask about. Authority: docs/evidence/D4/2026-09-28-pq-rag-unblock-misdescribed/ (E3, E4 and 'What rag needs' items 1, 2 and 4), under the founder decisions of 2026-09-28: the corpus is admitted ONLY through the existing Vault ingest path (routes/vault-ingest.ts -> ingestVaultDocument -> vault.document_chunks) into one dedicated evaluation organisation, with no second writer; gold items key to entries by document_code@version, resolved to vault document ids at run time; the PQ runs retrieval strategy 'basic' with reranking off. This data change and its proof are filed at docs/evidence/D4/2026-09-28-pq-rag-fail-closed/data/. STATUS: NOTHING HERE IS VERIFIED. On 2026-09-28 every issuer host was refused by the session's egress policy (see 'retrieval'), so no file was downloaded, no sha256 computed, no redistribution terms read, and no URL fetched. Titles, dates, versions and URLs come from the WebSearch index only and are kept in *Candidate(s) fields; the verified fields (sourceUrl, date, sha256) stay null and every version is provisional (versionVerified:false). An entry with verified:false must not be ingested for a PQ run, and a gold key must not resolve to it. See 'verifyProcedure' for how an entry becomes verified.
keyFormat: document_code@version. document_code and version are exactly what Vault ingest receives as documentCode and version, so the key maps 1:1 onto the vault upsert key (program_id, document_code, version) of the evaluation organisation's programme. A key is PROVISIONAL while its entry has versionVerified:false: verification re-pins version to the edition actually downloaded (see verifyProcedure step 3) and rewrites every gold key naming it in the same commit. gold-dataset.json keysProvisional says so on the gold side.

versionScheme.ICH: 'Step4': the ICH Step 4 text of that revision code, as published by ICH (not an EMA/FDA 'Step 5' re-publication, and not a Step 2 draft).
versionScheme.US-CFR: '<YYYY>-04-01': the govinfo annual edition of Title 21, revised as of April 1 of that year. The annual edition is the official legal edition; eCFR is not. All US-CFR entries pin ONE edition, the latest govinfo annual edition at verification.
versionScheme.US-Code: 'USCODE-<YYYY>': the govinfo edition of the United States Code. All US-Code entries pin ONE edition, the latest one govinfo has for every US-Code entry at verification.
versionScheme.FDA-guidance: 'final-<issue date as printed on the guidance>' (year-month, or year-month-day when the cover prints a day).
versionScheme.EU-CONS: 'CONS-<YYYY-MM-DD>': the EUR-Lex consolidated version of that date (CELEX 0<year>R<number>-<YYYYMMDD>). Pinned for acts amended or corrected since publication, because it shows the act as amended. EUR-Lex states that consolidated texts are documentation only and have no legal effect; the authentic texts are the Official Journal publications of the act and of each amending or correcting act. Verification checks every article a gold item relies on against those OJ texts (verifyProcedure step 3).
versionScheme.EU-OJ: 'OJ': the text as published in the Official Journal of the European Union. The electronic OJ on EUR-Lex is authentic only from 2013-07-01 (Council Regulation (EU) No 216/2013, per the search index); for an act published earlier, the printed OJ is authentic and EUR-Lex PDFs are reproductions. The OJ text shows no later amendment or corrigendum, so 'OJ' is used only for an act published from 2013-07-01 and not amended since.
versionScheme.UNPINNED: 'UNPINNED': the issuer's current revision could not be determined (the search index was contradictory). An UNPINNED entry is never keyed by a gold item and never ingested; verification replaces it with the revision printed on the document and moves the entry to its issuer's scheme.

admission.path: server/routes/vault-ingest.ts -> ingestVaultDocument (vault-ingest.service.ts) -> chunkDocumentForIngest -> INSERT INTO vault.document_chunks (document-chunking.service.ts)
admission.tenant: one dedicated evaluation organisation and one programme in it; document catalog and ana.vault_chunking enabled for that organisation only
admission.integrity: vault.documents.content_hash is sha256 of the uploaded bytes (vault-ingest.service.ts sha256Bytes); at run time it must equal this manifest's sha256 for the resolved key, or the item is unscored and the run is INCOMPLETE

failClosedRules: An entry with verified:false is not ingested for a PQ run.
A gold key that matches no entry here, or matches an entry with verified:false, does not resolve; the item is not scored and the rag component reports INCOMPLETE, never a numeric 0 read as FAIL.
A resolved vault document whose content_hash differs from sha256 here does not resolve.
Changing an entry's version changes its key; every gold key naming the old version must change in the same commit.

One entry is one file. A document_code@version identifies exactly one file and one sha256, and no two verified entries share a sha256. Where an issuer publishes one revision as separate files (ICH E6(R3): the principles and Annex 1, and Annex 2), each file gets its own document_code.
Within a scheme that is an edition of a code (US-CFR, US-Code), every entry pins the same edition.

Only an answer-source entry may be keyed by a gold item. A supporting or revision-distractor entry is ingested for retrieval realism but is never an expected source until its text has been read and it is re-roled.
An UNPINNED entry is never keyed and never ingested.
While any keyed entry has versionVerified:false, gold-dataset.json keysProvisional stays true.
A gold item with openChecks is not PQ-ready: it is not scored until each check is resolved from the verified text.
verifyProcedure: 1. From a network that can reach the issuer, open the issuer's own listing page and follow its link to the document. Record that URL in sourceUrl (for EU-CONS, the dated consolidated-version URL, not an undated ELI that resolves to whatever version is current).
2. Download the exact file. Record sha256 (hex, of the bytes as downloaded), retrievedAt and byte size.

3. Read the cover and confirm title, revision and date; record date and set versionVerified:true. Re-pin where the scheme says so: US-CFR to the latest govinfo annual edition of Title 21; US-Code to the latest edition govinfo has for every US-Code entry; EU-CONS to the latest consolidated version, after checking each article a gold item relies on against the OJ text of the act and of every amending or correcting act listed in the consolidated version. If the version changes, change it here and the matching keys in gold-dataset.json in the same commit.
4. Open the publisher's reuse terms page, quote the operative sentence into publishers.<publisher>.terms, record termsUrl and the date read, and set termsVerified:true.

5. Resolve every openChecks entry in gold-dataset.json that names this document, from the text just read; key a supporting entry only if its text answers the item, and re-role it answer-source when you do.
6. Set verified:true and write in 'verification' what was done and by whom. Do not set verified:true on any entry for which a step could not be done.
